correctness.rationale: The exact component enumeration and deletion bijection are elementary and independently reproduced for small carrier sizes. A saddle Boltzmann model with the correct q^2 zeta(q+1) leading mean and q^2(q+1) zeta(q+1) variance, Gaussian central arc, exponential outer arc and O(sigma^-1)=o(t) local shift error establishes the fixed-shift coefficient asymptotic. A finite-profile rank-r EF strategy plus finitely many canonical components gives the uniform sentence bound; a colour-1 singleton gives the matching nonzero constant. q=1 boundary, n=0 bookkeeping, fixed shifts and fixed ranks are explicit. Finite tests are not substituted for general proof.

originality.rationale: The final claim restricts novelty to the sharp quantitative all-first-order rate and exact leading singleton constant. Bell 2002 directly covers the qualitative zero–one assertion (even MSO), so it is explicitly credited rather than claimed as new. Burris et al. 1997 and Bell–Burris 2003 provide broad zero–one/ratio backgrounds, inspected to the stated material-access depth. Published-literature comparisons returned no dominating sharp coloured-star statement; older generalized-partition priority risks remain.
residual_risks: A general quantitative partition-ratio theorem could imply the fixed-shift estimate and permit a routine transfer to finite models; no such dominating all-FO rate was found, but absence of a search hit is not a proof of priority.
Bell 2002, Bell–Burris 2003 and full Koponen 2026 text were not all available for complete-document reading; this limits originality confidence.
The qualitative MSO 0–1 law is prior known and not part of the novel claim.

value.rationale: A sharp rate for every fixed first-order sentence and an explicit sharp witness give a meaningful quantitative strengthening of a general known zero–one law, not just another existence proof. The exponent 1/(q+1) changes systematically with the number of named colours and directly reflects growth of star component types. This is a natural minimal hierarchy model with an optimal analytic-logical boundary; precise invariant and reason for needing it are identified. No broad new theory or paper-sized result is claimed.
